A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in Spanish America, indigenous peoples resisted and rebelled against colonialism and Iberian hegemony, but that the resistance and rebellion were diverse and complex in their causes and manifestations, and that the colonial period was neither a "Pax Hispania" nor a "Pax Britannica."

resistance was an integral part of colonial life, that it varied in form from place to place, that it was often linked to material grievances, that it was not always a response to colonialism, that it was a form of social action, and that it often involved the use of religion.
the contributors to this volume have not yet reached consensus on the theoretical issues that underlie their research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the colonial period is a period of resistance, not of "pacification."
the Maya of Yucatan were not a passive or docile people, but that they resisted Spanish colonialism in various forms.
